_comment: Canonical adversarial corpus for ADR-0056 rule 1 (node id is a slug), run through EVERY
id guard in the family so rule 6/7's lockstep is a mechanical invariant instead of a
Consumers (each asserts the same verdict for the same id, in its own CI):
against `rule` by scripts/verify-twin-lockstep.py — that repo vendors nothing)
Verdicts only. Error TEXT parity is a per-twin-pair requirement (rule 7) and is asserted
in each pair's own tests; across languages the messages legitimately differ.
This file is the shared artifact. A vendored copy that differs from this one fails
scripts/verify-twin-lockstep.py, which is the point: weakening the corpus in one repo
must not be a quiet local decision.

vectors.why: real production id; a lowercase-only pattern would wrongly reject it
every legal punctuation character, none of them leading
exactly 100 characters — the boundary is inclusive
empty: there is no first character to be alphanumeric
leading dash: reads as a flag to anything that puts a bare id in an argv (dotclaude#47)
a lone dash is both leading-punctuation and a stdin sentinel
leading underscore: legal in the charset, illegal as a first character
NUL truncates the path at the syscall boundary
trailing newline — why the Python side uses fullmatch, not match
leading tilde expands to $HOME in a shell or under expanduser()
non-ASCII: the charset is ASCII by construction
Cyrillic а (U+0430) homoglyph — visually a legal id, byte-wise not
